what_it_is: First-generation Nextgen CLI: a TypeScript/Node scaffolder (inquirer + EJS + chalk) named nextgen-kit-cli v0.5. Generates Sanity 'section block' bundles for agency Next+Sanity sites: component, schema, page-builder schema, GROQ queries from EJS templates, driven by nextgen.config.json with configurable paths.
hardest_problems: Config-driven custom output paths ('Improving customPaths & Default')
Updating existing files at multiple marker points (update-file-with-multiple-markers.ts) - the marker idea originates here
Naming/blockType control for generated filenames

family_position: Generation 1 (2022): proved the scaffold-a-Sanity-block idea in TypeScript; its marker-based file-update trick became the family's core mechanism, and the Go rewrite superseded it in 2025.

what_it_is: nextgen-core-ui: a minimal React/Next.js layout component library (Section/InnerSection/Container/InnerContainer), Rollup-built, published to npm. 'Simplicity is the feature.'
hardest_problems: Getting a reusable layout-primitive API right (repeated Container/InnerSection iterations)
grade_why: Small npm library; shows the design-system instinct that later feeds nextgen-theme, but thin on its own.
family_position: Side branch (2023): the component vocabulary the CLI generates code against; superseded by shadcn-style starters and the nextgen-theme block library.

what_it_is: One-commit import of the Liveblocks Next.js Starter Kit (collaborative documents/whiteboard, auth, permissions). No custom work.
evidence: Single commit; stock Liveblocks starter README
family_position: Probe (Sep 2023): evaluated Liveblocks for the collaborative sitemap idea that became ng; the exploration moved there and this was never touched again.

what_it_is: Go CLI for creating Next.js app-router routes (static/dynamic/filler), well-tested (route_test, template_test, import_test), with release automation. Understands route grammar like app/(site)/[slug] and installs page/component templates into an existing tree.
frikk_role: Commissioner/product owner; implementation by contractor Suman Chapai.
status: Dormant since Feb 2024; superseded by nextgen-go-cli.
hardest_problems: Next.js route-grammar semantics (filler routes, dynamic segments named differently than [slug])
Idempotent import wiring in existing files
Template brace-escaping in generated JSX
evidence: README notes on filler routes and [slug] limitation

family_position: Generation 2 engine (2023-24): the first Go take on route generation, built to Frikk's spec by a contractor; its route-grammar lessons were absorbed into the 2025 solo Go rewrite.

Live multi-user tree state via Liveblocks
evidence: commit 4e61538 'Replace copy JSON section with copy ngo commands'

Pattern features / actionFile semantics for command templates

what_it_is: The flagship: a Go/Bubble Tea TUI + argument-driven CLI (npm-distributed as nextgen/ng/nextgen-cli, v1.0.147) that scaffolds Next+Sanity code from embedded JSON .nextgen templates. Idempotent marker-based insertion (requireAbsent, multi-line target matching, smartMerge), project auto-detection, persistent project registry, favorites/clipboard commands, file-tree previews, Clerk-backed auth for entitlements, ~150 automated releases.
status: Dormant since Sep 2025 but shipped and versioned (v1.0.147); the family's living center.
hardest_problems: Idempotent code injection into user-owned files: marker insertion with requireAbsent checks and multi-line target matching so re-runs never duplicate (commits 95d2ef6, b814da7, 0698f7e)
smartMerge of snippets into existing TS/TSX while preserving formatting without a real AST
One codebase serving both an interactive TUI and a scriptable, AI-agent-safe argument CLI
Cross-platform Go binary shipped through npm with four bin aliases
CLI device-link auth flow against the nextgen-theme dashboard (Clerk entitlements)

what_it_is: The nextgen family is one sustained attack on a single agency pain: hand-wiring Next.js + Sanity page-builder code - every new block or route means a component, a schema, GROQ queries, and registry/import edits scattered across files. Generation 1 (Nextgen-CLI, 2022-23, TypeScript/EJS) proved the scaffold and invented the family's core primitive: marker comments that let a generator idempotently edit files it doesn't own. Nextgen-UI supplied the layout vocabulary. Generation 2 (2023-24) outsourced an engine rewrite to contractor Suman Chapai - ngo (tested Go route generator with real route-grammar semantics: filler routes, dynamic segments), ng (Liveblocks collaborative sitemap builder emitting ngo commands), and the Wails desktop apps ngui/nextgen-on-wails, where Frikk co-wrote Go for the first time. Lesson: GUIs over codegen are heavy; the route grammar and Go were keepers. Generation 3 (2025) is the convergence: nextgen-go-cli, a 335-commit solo Go/Bubble Tea TUI + argument-driven CLI, npm-distributed, v1.0.147, with requireAbsent marker merging, project auto-detection, and Clerk entitlements - flanked by nextgen-theme (Stripe dashboard, CLI device-link licensing - the business attempt) and the testgen dogfood ranges (testgen-9 ran seven months on a real site; testgen-5 mutated into a Monaco-based template-editor prototype). Generation 4 (late 2025) moved into the editor: nextgen-markers (marker lists, decorations, Windows hardening) and nextgen-vscode (LSP, formatter, diagnostics for .nextgen as a language). The family has been quiet since October 2025: a shipped, versioned CLI with a built-but-unlaunched commercial layer and a promising editor beachhead.
